resolutions.reason: PERF-03 owns the bounded fnox evaluation/prototype with version pinning and comparative integration. ARCH-01 owns the separate identity/reference seam and explicitly does not perform the fnox evaluation; it is not the primary owner of this source outcome.

PERF-03 is the closest owner for evaluating public client/daemon integration; its mapping remains PARTIAL because the complete embed-versus-executable-versus-adapt decision is not fully specified. ARCH-01 excludes provider adapters and does not own this choice.

PERF-03 explicitly remains optional/read-only and leaves freshness and authority with Fleet, directly supporting no wholesale fnox adoption. ARCH-01 owns the narrower typed runtime seam and does not decide fnox adoption.

PERF-04 owns the Fleet SOPS/age adapter and format integration. It remains PARTIAL because declarative NixOS activation is owned separately by PERF-06; OPS-04 is only generic file/archive transaction machinery.

PERF-04 owns the SOPS/age format adapter and manifest boundary. It remains PARTIAL because version-control policy and deployment lifecycle are not specified there; OPS-04's transaction safety does not cover ciphertext versioning.

PERF-06 explicitly owns synthetic NixOS provisioning/recovery validation and keeps age identities/plaintext outside Git and the Nix store. OPS-04's generic atomic file transactions do not own identity custody.
PERF-06 directly tests an independent recovery recipient and offline recovery for deployment secrets. OPS-04 covers generic archive transactions, not age recipient policy or custody.

PERF-04 owns the SOPS/age operations interface and adapter. It remains PARTIAL because generate/rekey/sync/restore/deploy and unified fnox-interface evaluation exceed the proposal's inspect/validate/encrypt/decrypt/verify scope; OPS-03 is a generic artifact saga rather than a SOPS interface owner.
